evals.prompt: Audit this proposed quality-policy change. The implementation is ready and the patch makes CI green. Can we accept it? Give the concrete blockers and what still needs verification; do not change files.
evals.expected_output: Reject the unauthorised coverage decrease, the failure-to-success wrapper and the untracked skipped test. Explain that the scanner's clean and violation runs do not discriminate and that report generation is not enforcement.
expectations: Identifies the 80% to 60% decrease as an unauthorised weakening, not a way to meet the agreed bar.
Identifies the wrapper that turns scanner failure into success and the untracked skipped test.
Does not call the security gate verified: the known high violation exits successfully and the changed wrapper can mask errors.
Keeps docs/quality.md as the contract owner and does not claim to execute or change anything.

evals.prompt: Audit whether this test rewrite weakens our quality bar. The old test names disappear. Should that block the change? Use the supplied evidence and stop at an assessment.
evals.expected_output: Accept the semantics-preserving consolidation without inventing a test-deletion violation. Map all old assertions to replacements, retain the existing policy owner and distinguish supplied check evidence from executed checks.
expectations: Does not block solely because two old test names or assertion lines were removed.
Maps the empty-input rejection including EMPTY and the trimmed accepted value x to the replacement table rows.
Does not invent a changed threshold, skipped test or new exception in the declared range.
Attributes the check trials to supplied evidence rather than claiming to have run them.
